column3: Although 容易 means easy, the phrase means it was hard, and the shorter 好容易 means exactly the same. It usually comes before 才, as in 好不容易才找到, to say you finally managed it.
column4: 我好不容易才找到这家店。
column5: 我好不容易才找到這家店。
column6: Wǒ hǎobùróngyì cái zhǎodào zhè jiā diàn.
column7: I had a hard time finding this shop.
column9: Although 容易 means easy, the phrase means it was hard, and the shorter 好容易 means exactly the same. It usually comes before 才, as in 好不容易才找到, to say you finally managed it.

column3: Very common as a polite excuse when you can't come or must leave (我有事, 先走了). 没事 is the opposite: nothing is wrong, never mind.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yǒushì, bù néng qù.
column7: I have something to do today, so I can't go.
column9: Very common as a polite excuse when you can't come or must leave (我有事, 先走了). 沒事 is the opposite: nothing is wrong, never mind.

column3: Mostly inside words: 爆炸 (explode), 爆米花 (popcorn), 爆红 (go viral). In cooking, 爆炒 means to stir-fry fast over high heat.
column6: Qìqiú bào le.
column7: The balloon burst.
column9: Mostly inside words: 爆炸 (explode), 爆米花 (popcorn), 爆紅 (go viral). In cooking, 爆炒 means to stir-fry fast over high heat.

column3: Rare on its own in speech, where mother is 妈妈; it lives in compounds such as 母亲, 母语 (mother tongue) and 母校 (one's old school), and 母的 says that an animal is female. It is 女, woman, with extra dots added to set it apart.
column4: 这只猫是公的还是母的？
column5: 這隻貓是公的還是母的？
column6: Zhè zhī māo shì gōng de háishi mǔ de?
column7: Is this cat a male or a female?
column9: Rare on its own in speech, where mother is 媽媽; it lives in compounds such as 母親, 母語 (mother tongue) and 母校 (one's old school), and 母的 says that an animal is female. It is 女, woman, with extra dots added to set it apart.

column3: Often used as 以…出名 (famous for…), and a person or place can be 出名 for something bad as well as good.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn yǐ niúròumiàn chūmíng.
column7: This shop is famous for its beef noodles.
column9: Often used as 以…出名 (famous for…), and a person or place can be 出名 for something bad as well as good.

column3: Also a very common spoken intensifier before an adjective, as in 超好吃 and 超贵; it is informal and typical of younger speakers.
column6: Zhè jiā de dàngāo chāo hǎochī.
column7: This place's cake is super delicious.
column9: Also a very common spoken intensifier before an adjective, as in 超好吃 and 超貴; it is informal and typical of younger speakers.

column3: A fixed pair for 'at home and abroad', used before a noun or after a word like 驰名, as in 驰名中外 (famous everywhere) and 中外合资 (a joint venture).
column4: 这座古城吸引了中外游客。
column5: 這座古城吸引了中外遊客。
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng xīyǐn le zhōngwài yóukè.
column7: This old city attracts visitors from China and abroad.
column9: A fixed pair for 'at home and abroad', used before a noun or after a word like 馳名, as in 馳名中外 (famous everywhere) and 中外合資 (a joint venture).

column3: The middle stretch of a period or process, such as a project, a plan or an illness; the neighbors are 前期 (early) and 后期 (late).
column4: 这个项目已经进入中期。
column5: 這個項目已經進入中期。
column6: Zhège xiàngmù yǐjīng jìnrù zhōngqī.
column7: The project has reached its middle phase.
column9: The middle stretch of a period or process, such as a project, a plan or an illness; the neighbors are 前期 (early) and 後期 (late).

column3: Two uses: living things growing back or being reborn (再生能力 is the power to regenerate), and recycling, as in 再生纸 (recycled paper) and 可再生能源 (renewable energy).
column4: 可再生能源越来越重要。
column5: 可再生能源越來越重要。
column6: Kě zàishēng néngyuán yuè lái yuè zhòngyào.
column7: Renewable energy is getting more and more important.
column9: Two uses: living things growing back or being reborn (再生能力 is the power to regenerate), and recycling, as in 再生紙 (recycled paper) and 可再生能源 (renewable energy).

column3: It takes something gradually used up as its object: 消耗能量, 消耗体力, 消耗时间 (energy, strength, time). It fits calories and fuel too. The old meaning "news" is rare today. 耗 was originally written differently.
column6: Pǎobù huì xiāohào hěn duō rèliàng.
column7: Running burns a lot of calories.
column9: It takes something gradually used up as its object: 消耗能量, 消耗體力, 消耗時間 (energy, strength, time). It fits calories and fuel too. The old meaning "news" is rare today. 耗 was originally written differently.

column3: Mother and daughter as a pair. 母女俩 means the two of them together. The pair of mother and son is 母子. 母 is 女 with dots added to tell the two apart.
column6: Tāmen mǔnǚ liǎ zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
column7: The mother and daughter look very much alike.
column9: Mother and daughter as a pair. 母女倆 means the two of them together. The pair of mother and son is 母子. 母 is 女 with dots added to tell the two apart.

column3: Mother and son as a pair: 母子俩. Also used of a mother and her baby, as in 母子平安, after a birth.
column6: Mǔzǐ píng'ān, qǐng fàngxīn.
column7: Mother and baby are both safe, so please do not worry.
column9: Mother and son as a pair: 母子倆. Also used of a mother and her baby, as in 母子平安, after a birth.

column3: Names the pair as a unit, as in 父子关系 for their relationship; 父子俩 means the two of them together. 父 began as a picture of a hand holding a stone blade, a man working with a stone axe.
column6: Fùzǐ zhījiān méiyǒu mìmì.
column7: Between father and son there are no secrets.
column9: Names the pair as a unit, as in 父子關係 for their relationship; 父子倆 means the two of them together. 父 began as a picture of a hand holding a stone blade, a man working with a stone axe.

column3: Names the pair as a unit, like 父子 and 母女; 父女俩 means the two of them together. 女 pictures a woman with folded arms, kneeling or standing.
column4: 这对父女经常一起去公园。
column5: 這對父女經常一起去公園。
column6: Zhè duì fùnǚ jīngcháng yīqǐ qù gōngyuán.
column7: This father and daughter often go to the park together.
column9: Names the pair as a unit, like 父子 and 母女; 父女倆 means the two of them together. 女 pictures a woman with folded arms, kneeling or standing.

column3: Relatives by blood or marriage, in legal and official wording (亲属关系, 死者亲属); in everyday talk people say 亲戚.
column6: Qǐng tōngzhī bìngrén de qīnshǔ.
column7: Please notify the patient's relatives.
column9: Relatives by blood or marriage, in legal and official wording (親屬關係, 死者親屬); in everyday talk people say 親戚.

column3: Used for a child who has lost their parents; 孤儿院 is an orphanage. 儿 is a picture of an infant, showing the soft spot of its skull.
column4: 这个孤儿是奶奶养大的。
column5: 這個孤兒是奶奶養大的。
column6: Zhège gū'ér shì nǎinai yǎng dà de.
column7: This orphan was raised by his grandmother.
column9: Used for a child who has lost their parents; 孤兒院 is an orphanage. 兒 is a picture of an infant, showing the soft spot of its skull.

column3: Found mainly in labels for things made for children (少儿节目, 少儿英语, 少儿读物); in speech a child is 孩子. 少 is drawn as a few dots, perhaps grains of sand.
column4: 这家书店有很多少儿读物。
column5: 這家書店有很多少兒讀物。
column6: Zhè jiā shūdiàn yǒu hěn duō shào'ér dúwù.
column7: This bookstore has many books for children.
column9: Found mainly in labels for things made for children (少兒節目, 少兒英語, 少兒讀物); in speech a child is 孩子. 少 is drawn as a few dots, perhaps grains of sand.

column3: Two common uses: a newcomer at a company or in a field (职场新人), and a newlywed, especially the bride and groom at their wedding. 新 began as the word for chopping firewood and was later borrowed for "new".
column6: Xīnrén zhèngzài xiàng kèrén jìng jiǔ.
column7: The bride and groom are toasting the guests.
column9: Two common uses: a newcomer at a company or in a field (職場新人), and a newlywed, especially the bride and groom at their wedding. 新 began as the word for chopping firewood and was later borrowed for "new".

column3: Someone whose help at a critical time you owe a debt of gratitude for; 救命恩人 is the person who saved your life.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de jiùmìng ēnrén.
column7: He is the person who saved my life.
column9: Someone whose help at a critical time you owe a debt of gratitude for; 救命恩人 is the person who saved your life.

column3: Someone from your own home region, a bond that counts most when you meet far from home; also a friendly way to address a country person you don't know. 老 shows an old man with long hair, leaning on a cane.
column4: 在国外遇到老乡，我特别高兴。
column5: 在國外遇到老鄉，我特別高興。
column6: Zài guówài yùdào lǎoxiāng, wǒ tèbié gāoxìng.
column7: I was especially happy to meet someone from my hometown abroad.
column9: Someone from your own home region, a bond that counts most when you meet far from home; also a friendly way to address a country person you don't know. 老 shows an old man with long hair, leaning on a cane.

column3: Plain "rich people" as a group; the opposite is 穷人, and 富人区 is a wealthy neighborhood.
column4: 富人和穷人的生活差别很大。
column5: 富人和窮人的生活差別很大。
column6: Fùrén hé qióngrén de shēnghuó chābié hěn dà.
column7: The lives of the rich and the poor differ a great deal.
column9: Plain "rich people" as a group; the opposite is 窮人, and 富人區 is a wealthy neighborhood.

column3: The standard, neutral word for a blind person; related words include 盲道 (tactile paving) and 盲文 (braille).
column6: Mángrén yòng shǒu mō mángwén.
column7: Blind people read braille with their hands.
column9: The standard, neutral word for a blind person; related words include 盲道 (tactile paving) and 盲文 (braille).

column3: Describes a lasting disability of body or senses, either said of a person (他有残疾) or in compounds such as 残疾人 and 残疾证. 疾 also meant "fast", from an arrow flying toward a person; the two meanings ended up in one character.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù yǒu cánjí.
column7: He has had a disability since childhood.
column9: Describes a lasting disability of body or senses, either said of a person (他有殘疾) or in compounds such as 殘疾人 and 殘疾證. 疾 also meant "fast", from an arrow flying toward a person; the two meanings ended up in one character.

column3: The standard term on the mainland, in signs and official language, such as 残疾人专用 on a parking space or restroom. In Taiwan the official word is 身心障碍者 (身障), as in 身障专用.
column4: 这里是残疾人专用车位。
column5: 這裡是殘疾人專用車位。
column6: Zhèlǐ shì cánjírén zhuānyòng chēwèi.
column7: This is a parking space reserved for people with disabilities.
column9: The standard term on the mainland, in signs and official language, such as 殘疾人專用 on a parking space or restroom. In Taiwan the official word is 身心障礙者 (身障), as in 身障專用.

column3: Visitors strolling around a park or scenic spot, as on signs and in guidebooks (游人止步 "visitors, no entry"). The right part of 游 also hints at travelling.
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yóurén hěn duō.
column7: There are lots of visitors in the park.
column9: Visitors strolling around a park or scenic spot, as on signs and in guidebooks (遊人止步 "visitors, no entry"). The right part of 遊 also hints at travelling.

column3: A learner in a course or training program, such as a driving school, a sports club or military training; for a school pupil say 学生.
column4: 这位教练有二十个学员。
column5: 這位教練有二十個學員。
column6: Zhè wèi jiàoliàn yǒu èrshí gè xuéyuán.
column7: This coach has twenty trainees.
column9: A learner in a course or training program, such as a driving school, a sports club or military training; for a school pupil say 學生.

column3: Wounded people in a disaster, battle or accident report, usually as a group: 救治伤员 means to treat the wounded.
column6: Yīshēng zhèngzài jiùzhì shāngyuán.
column7: The doctors are treating the wounded.
column9: Wounded people in a disaster, battle or accident report, usually as a group: 救治傷員 means to treat the wounded.

column3: A medical word for someone suffering from an illness, as in clinics and news reports (癌症患者, 糖尿病患者); in conversation people say 病人. 者 works like English -er: one who does or is something.
column4: 这种药适合糖尿病患者。
column5: 這種藥適合糖尿病患者。
column6: Zhè zhǒng yào shìhé tángniàobìng huànzhě.
column7: This medicine suits people with diabetes.
column9: A medical word for someone suffering from an illness, as in clinics and news reports (癌症患者, 糖尿病患者); in conversation people say 病人. 者 works like English -er: one who does or is something.

column3: Teachers and students taken together, as in 师生关系 and 全校师生 (everyone at the school).
column4: 全校师生都参加了典礼。
column5: 全校師生都參加了典禮。
column6: Quánxiào shīshēng dōu cānjiā le diǎnlǐ.
column7: All the teachers and students of the school took part in the ceremony.
column9: Teachers and students taken together, as in 師生關係 and 全校師生 (everyone at the school).

column3: A title of respect for a master of an art or discipline (国画大师, 武术大师), and in chess a grandmaster; also used for a Buddhist master.
column6: Tā shì yī wèi guóhuà dàshī.
column7: He is a master of Chinese painting.
column9: A title of respect for a master of an art or discipline (國畫大師, 武術大師), and in chess a grandmaster; also used for a Buddhist master.

column3: Top leaders of states or governments, mostly in 国家首脑 and 首脑会议 (a summit); not used for the head of a company. 首 began as a picture of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns.
column6: Liǎng guó shǒunǎo jiāng jǔxíng huìtán.
column7: The leaders of the two countries will hold talks.
column9: Top leaders of states or governments, mostly in 國家首腦 and 首腦會議 (a summit); not used for the head of a company. 首 began as a picture of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns.

column3: A job title: put the field before it, as in 服装设计师 and 室内设计师; 师 is the same ending as in 工程师 and 医师.
column6: Tā shì yī míng shìnèi shèjìshī.
column7: She is an interior designer.
column9: A job title: put the field before it, as in 服裝設計師 and 室內設計師; 師 is the same ending as in 工程師 and 醫師.

column3: The ordinary job title for a street sweeper or building cleaner; 工 marks a manual worker, as in 电工 and 民工.
column4: 清洁工每天早上五点就开始扫街。
column5: 清潔工每天早上五點就開始掃街。
column6: Qīngjiégōng měitiān zǎoshang wǔ diǎn jiù kāishǐ sǎo jiē.
column7: The cleaner starts sweeping the streets at five every morning.
column9: The ordinary job title for a street sweeper or building cleaner; 工 marks a manual worker, as in 電工 and 民工.

column3: Short for 人民警察, the ordinary police officer on the mainland, as seen on the street or at a local station.
column6: Mínjǐng zhèngzài wéichí zhìxù.
column7: The police officer is keeping order.
column9: Short for 人民警察, the ordinary police officer on the mainland, as seen on the street or at a local station.

column3: A worker from the countryside doing construction or other manual work in a city; the full form is 农民工.
column4: 许多民工春节才能回家。
column5: 許多民工春節才能回家。
column6: Xǔduō míngōng Chūnjié cái néng huí jiā.
column7: Many migrant workers can only go home at the Spring Festival.
column9: A worker from the countryside doing construction or other manual work in a city; the full form is 農民工.

column3: Read tóngháng, someone in the same trade, a peer in your field though not necessarily your coworker; the same characters read tóngxíng mean to travel together. 行 began as a picture of a street intersection and was later borrowed for "to go".
column4: 同行之间应该互相帮助。
column5: 同行之間應該互相幫助。
column6: Tóngháng zhījiān yīnggāi hùxiāng bāngzhù.
column7: People in the same trade should help one another.
column9: Read tóngháng, someone in the same trade, a peer in your field though not necessarily your coworker; the same characters read tóngxíng mean to travel together. 行 began as a picture of a street intersection and was later borrowed for "to go".

column3: Office workers; the opposite is 蓝领, and it also works as a modifier, as in 白领阶层 (the white-collar class). 领 is a word for neck and collar that also grew into "to lead".
column4: 很多白领中午都在公司附近吃饭。
column5: 很多白領中午都在公司附近吃飯。
column6: Hěn duō báilǐng zhōngwǔ dōu zài gōngsī fùjìn chīfàn.
column7: Many office workers eat lunch near the company at noon.
column9: Office workers; the opposite is 藍領, and it also works as a modifier, as in 白領階層 (the white-collar class). 領 is a word for neck and collar that also grew into "to lead".

column3: Factory and manual workers, the counterpart of 白领: 蓝领工人. 蓝 comes from a word for indigo.
column4: 这家工厂里蓝领的工资不低。
column5: 這家工廠裡藍領的工資不低。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng lǐ lánlǐng de gōngzī bù dī.
column7: Blue-collar workers in this factory are not badly paid.
column9: Factory and manual workers, the counterpart of 白領: 藍領工人. 藍 comes from a word for indigo.

column3: Someone who speaks officially for an organization, as in 外交部发言人 and 新闻发言人; it can also mean whoever is speaking at a meeting. 发 began as a picture of a bow firing an arrow.
column4: 外交部发言人回答了记者的问题。
column5: 外交部發言人回答了記者的問題。
column6: Wàijiāobù fāyánrén huídá le jìzhě de wèntí.
column7: The foreign ministry spokesperson answered the reporters' questions.
column9: Someone who speaks officially for an organization, as in 外交部發言人 and 新聞發言人; it can also mean whoever is speaking at a meeting. 發 began as a picture of a bow firing an arrow.

column3: The host of a TV or radio show, an event or a meeting (电视主持人, 节目主持人); the verb behind it is 主持.
column4: 这位主持人很受观众欢迎。
column5: 這位主持人很受觀眾歡迎。
column6: Zhè wèi zhǔchírén hěn shòu guānzhòng huānyíng.
column7: This host is very popular with viewers.
column9: The host of a TV or radio show, an event or a meeting (電視主持人, 節目主持人); the verb behind it is 主持.

column3: Someone learning a trade or craft under a 师傅 (the master); 收徒弟 means to take on an apprentice. 弟 began as a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping meant order, which led to "younger brother".
column4: 师傅正在教徒弟做面条。
column5: 師傅正在教徒弟做麵條。
column6: Shīfu zhèngzài jiāo túdì zuò miàntiáo.
column7: The master is teaching his apprentice to make noodles.
column9: Someone learning a trade or craft under a 師傅 (the master); 收徒弟 means to take on an apprentice. 弟 began as a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping meant order, which led to "younger brother".

column3: Husked rice as a staple, the grain you buy by the bag; once cooked it is called 米饭. 米 is a picture of rice kernels without the husk.
column4: 我们家每个月买二十斤大米。
column5: 我們家每個月買二十斤大米。
column6: Wǒmen jiā měi gè yuè mǎi èrshí jīn dàmǐ.
column7: Our family buys twenty jin of rice every month.
column9: Husked rice as a staple, the grain you buy by the bag; once cooked it is called 米飯. 米 is a picture of rice kernels without the husk.

column3: The packaged snack of thin fried slices; in Taiwan usually 洋芋片. Hot chips served as a side are 薯条.
column4: 他一边看电视一边吃薯片。
column5: 他一邊看電視一邊吃薯片。
column6: Tā yībiān kàn diànshì yībiān chī shǔpiàn.
column7: He eats potato chips while watching TV.
column9: The packaged snack of thin fried slices; in Taiwan usually 洋芋片. Hot chips served as a side are 薯條.

column3: In northern China the everyday word is usually 西红柿, while 番茄 is usual in the south and in Taiwan; everyone says 番茄酱 for ketchup and 番茄炒蛋 for the egg-and-tomato stir-fry.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan chī fānqié chǎo dàn.
column7: I like eating tomato and scrambled eggs.
column9: In northern China the everyday word is usually 西紅柿, while 番茄 is usual in the south and in Taiwan; everyone says 番茄醬 for ketchup and 番茄炒蛋 for the egg-and-tomato stir-fry.

column3: Besides the vegetable, 茄子! is what people say to the camera, just like "cheese!" in English, and the photographer often calls it out to get everyone smiling.
column4: 红烧茄子是一道家常菜。
column5: 紅燒茄子是一道家常菜。
column6: Hóngshāo qiézi shì yī dào jiācháng cài.
column7: Braised eggplant is a home-style dish.
column9: Besides the vegetable, 茄子! is what people say to the camera, just like "cheese!" in English, and the photographer often calls it out to get everyone smiling.

column3: Dairy as a food category on labels and in shops, covering milk, cheese and yogurt; 乳 is mostly a written element, while plain milk is 牛奶. 乳 began as a kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child.
column6: Tā duì rǔzhìpǐn guòmǐn.
column7: He is allergic to dairy products.
column9: Dairy as a food category on labels and in shops, covering milk, cheese and yogurt; 乳 is mostly a written element, while plain milk is 牛奶. 乳 began as a kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child.

column3: A thick paste or sauce; it ends many names, such as 辣椒酱, 番茄酱 and 花生酱, and on its own suggests a savory soy-based paste.
column6: Zhège cài lǐ fàng le hěn duō jiàng.
column7: A lot of sauce went into this dish.
column9: A thick paste or sauce; it ends many names, such as 辣椒醬, 番茄醬 and 花生醬, and on its own suggests a savory soy-based paste.

column3: Jam, spread on bread or toast; the fruit comes first: 草莓果酱, 蓝莓果酱. 果 is a picture of fruits on a tree.
column6: Tā zài miànbāo shàng tú le guǒjiàng.
column7: She spread jam on the bread.
column9: Jam, spread on bread or toast; the fruit comes first: 草莓果醬, 藍莓果醬. 果 is a picture of fruits on a tree.

column3: All the drinks together, alcoholic or not, as on a restaurant menu or a banquet bill; 酒水单 is the drinks list. 酒 was first written 酉, and 水 was added later to tell it apart.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de jiǔshuǐ hěn guì.
column7: The drinks at this restaurant are expensive.
column9: All the drinks together, alcoholic or not, as on a restaurant menu or a banquet bill; 酒水單 is the drinks list. 酒 was first written 酉, and 水 was added later to tell it apart.

column3: In speech 勺子 is more usual; 勺 is seen in compounds such as 汤勺 (soup ladle) and as a measure word, 一勺盐. 勺 shows wine in a ladle or spoon.
column6: Zài jiā yī sháo yán.
column7: Add one more spoonful of salt.
column9: In speech 勺子 is more usual; 勺 is seen in compounds such as 湯勺 (soup ladle) and as a measure word, 一勺鹽. 勺 shows wine in a ladle or spoon.

column3: Goes with 用 and a verb: 用微波炉热饭 means to heat food in the microwave.
column4: 把饭放进微波炉里热一下。
column5: 把飯放進微波爐裡熱一下。
column6: Bǎ fàn fàng jìn wēibōlú lǐ rè yīxià.
column7: Put the rice in the microwave and heat it up.
column9: Goes with 用 and a verb: 用微波爐熱飯 means to heat food in the microwave.

column3: Plain cold, unboiled water straight from the tap; 洗冷水澡 is to take a cold shower.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan xǐ lěngshuǐ zǎo.
column7: In summer I like taking cold showers.
column9: Plain cold, unboiled water straight from the tap; 洗冷水澡 is to take a cold shower.

column3: Usually with 有, 没有 or verbs such as 增加 and 影响; 胃口 is a more colloquial near-synonym. 食 shows a mouth over a bowl of rice on a stand.
column6: Tiānqì tài rè, wǒ méiyǒu shíyù.
column7: The weather is so hot that I have no appetite.
column9: Usually with 有, 沒有 or verbs such as 增加 and 影響; 胃口 is a more colloquial near-synonym. 食 shows a mouth over a bowl of rice on a stand.

column3: A building of several stories, in contrast to a 平房 (a single-story house).
column6: Zhèlǐ xīn jiàn le hěn duō lóufáng.
column7: Many new buildings have been put up here.
column9: A building of several stories, in contrast to a 平房 (a single-story house).

column3: The shared hallway or stairwell inside an apartment building, a mainland word; in Taiwan people say 楼梯间 or 走廊. 道 is possibly a head walking on a road.
column6: Lóudào lǐ de dēng huài le.
column7: The light in the stairwell is broken.
column9: The shared hallway or stairwell inside an apartment building, a mainland word; in Taiwan people say 樓梯間 or 走廊. 道 is possibly a head walking on a road.

column3: A basement, often used for storage or parking; 地下 on its own means underground. 室 first meant a house or residence.
column4: 我们把旧家具放在地下室。
column5: 我們把舊家具放在地下室。
column6: Wǒmen bǎ jiù jiājù fàng zài dìxiàshì.
column7: We keep the old furniture in the basement.
column9: A basement, often used for storage or parking; 地下 on its own means underground. 室 first meant a house or residence.

column3: The measure word is 根: 一根柱子; on its own 柱 mostly appears in compounds such as 石柱 and 支柱. 柱 is related to 拄, which means "to support".
column4: 屋子中间有一根大柱子。
column5: 屋子中間有一根大柱子。
column6: Wūzi zhōngjiān yǒu yī gēn dà zhùzi.
column7: There is a big pillar in the middle of the room.
column9: The measure word is 根: 一根柱子; on its own 柱 mostly appears in compounds such as 石柱 and 支柱. 柱 is related to 拄, which means "to support".

column3: Home as a place you belong to and care for, such as a homeland or a community: 重建家园 is to rebuild after a disaster; warmer and more literary than 家.
column4: 地震以后，人们开始重建家园。
column5: 地震以後，人們開始重建家園。
column6: Dìzhèn yǐhòu, rénmen kāishǐ chóngjiàn jiāyuán.
column7: After the earthquake, people began to rebuild their homes.
column9: Home as a place you belong to and care for, such as a homeland or a community: 重建家園 is to rebuild after a disaster; warmer and more literary than 家.

column3: Cement, the gray powder; mixed with sand and water it makes 混凝土 (concrete), and 水泥路 is a concrete road.
column6: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài pū shuǐní lù.
column7: The workers are paving a cement road.
column9: Cement, the gray powder; mixed with sand and water it makes 混凝土 (concrete), and 水泥路 is a concrete road.

column3: Common on signs and in job titles for cleaning work, such as 清洁工 (cleaner) and 清洁剂 (cleaning product).
column6: Qǐng bǎochí jiàoshì qīngjié.
column7: Please keep the classroom clean.
column9: Common on signs and in job titles for cleaning work, such as 清潔工 (cleaner) and 清潔劑 (cleaning product).

column3: Washing something thoroughly until it is clean, usually an object, a wound or a surface: 清洗伤口, 清洗油烟机. Plain 洗 is the everyday word for washing hands or clothes.
column6: Yòng qīngshuǐ qīngxǐ shāngkǒu.
column7: Rinse the wound with clean water.
column9: Washing something thoroughly until it is clean, usually an object, a wound or a surface: 清洗傷口, 清洗油煙機. Plain 洗 is the everyday word for washing hands or clothes.

column3: For clean it lives inside words such as 干净 and 净化. On its own before a verb or noun it means nothing but: 净说空话 is nothing but empty talk. It is probably related to 清, which also means clean and pure.
column6: Tā jìng shuō hǎotīng de.
column7: He says nothing but nice things.
column9: For clean it lives inside words such as 乾淨 and 淨化. On its own before a verb or noun it means nothing but: 淨說空話 is nothing but empty talk. It is probably related to 清, which also means clean and pure.

column3: A coat or jacket worn over other clothes. It is also used figuratively for a disguise, as in 披着…的外衣 (cloaked in the guise of). 衣 is a picture of the outline of the chest and upper clothing.
column4: 天气冷了，你把外衣穿上吧。
column5: 天氣冷了，你把外衣穿上吧。
column6: Tiānqì lěng le, nǐ bǎ wàiyī chuān shàng ba.
column7: It has turned cold, so put your coat on.
column9: A coat or jacket worn over other clothes. It is also used figuratively for a disguise, as in 披著…的外衣 (cloaked in the guise of). 衣 is a picture of the outline of the chest and upper clothing.

column3: Fashionable, new-season clothes, as in 时装店 (fashion boutique) and 时装秀 (fashion show). Clothes in general are 衣服.
column4: 这家店卖的时装很漂亮。
column5: 這家店賣的時裝很漂亮。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài de shízhuāng hěn piàoliang.
column7: The fashions this shop sells are very pretty.
column9: Fashionable, new-season clothes, as in 時裝店 (fashion boutique) and 時裝秀 (fashion show). Clothes in general are 衣服.

column3: A modifier for pocket-sized versions of things: 袖珍词典 (pocket dictionary), 袖珍收音机 (pocket radio). It does not stand for sleeves in general. 珍 first meant a gemstone, and later also came to mean rare.
column6: Tā yǒu yī běn xiùzhēn cídiǎn.
column7: He has a pocket dictionary.
column9: A modifier for pocket-sized versions of things: 袖珍詞典 (pocket dictionary), 袖珍收音機 (pocket radio). It does not stand for sleeves in general. 珍 first meant a gemstone, and later also came to mean rare.

column3: Jewelry as merchandise or valuables: 珠宝店 is a jewelry store and 珠宝首饰 covers jewelry in general. 宝 once showed a house with jade and a cowry shell inside: treasures in a house.
column6: Tā dàizhe hěn duō zhūbǎo.
column7: She is wearing a lot of jewelry.
column9: Jewelry as merchandise or valuables: 珠寶店 is a jewelry store and 珠寶首飾 covers jewelry in general. 寶 once showed a house with jade and a cowry shell inside: treasures in a house.

column3: As a verb it goes with the thing made: 织毛衣 (knit a sweater), 织布 (weave cloth). It is also the second half of 纺织 (textiles). 织 comes from a form with silk 糸 as its meaning part, and its right half was cut down to 只.
column6: Nǎinai zài zhī máoyī.
column7: Grandma is knitting a sweater.
column9: As a verb it goes with the thing made: 織毛衣 (knit a sweater), 織布 (weave cloth). It is also the second half of 紡織 (textiles). 織 has silk 糸 as its meaning part.

column3: Beauty care for the face and skin. It is a verb-object word, so you go to 美容院 (a beauty salon) or 做美容 (have a beauty treatment). 美 began as a picture of a person wearing a headdress of feathers or a ram's horn.
column6: Tā měi gè yuè dōu qù zuò měiróng.
column7: She goes for a beauty treatment every month.
column9: Beauty care for the face and skin. It is a verb-object word, so you go to 美容院 (a beauty salon) or 做美容 (have a beauty treatment). 美 began as a picture of a person wearing a headdress of feathers or a ram's horn.

column3: Found inside words such as 特别, 特点 and 特价. On its own before an adjective it is colloquial for "really, very": 特好, 特美. It meant a large bull, hence the ox 牛 inside; the sense of unique may be an extension of that, since a bull is large.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng tè měi.
column7: The scenery here is especially beautiful.
column9: Found inside words such as 特別, 特點 and 特價. On its own before an adjective it is colloquial for "really, very": 特好, 特美. It meant a large bull, hence the ox 牛 inside; the sense of unique may be an extension of that, since a bull is large.

column3: Doing something on purpose for someone or for a reason, usually out of kindness or effort. For doing something deliberately in a bad sense, 故意 is the word.
column6: Wǒ tèyì gěi nǐ dài le kāfēi.
column7: I brought you coffee on purpose.
column9: Doing something on purpose for someone or for a reason, usually out of kindness or effort. For doing something deliberately in a bad sense, 故意 is the word.

column3: Works both as an adjective (极端天气 is extreme weather) and as a noun: 走极端 means to go to extremes. 极 originally meant a crossbeam rafter.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ tài jíduān le.
column7: His way of thinking is too extreme.
column9: Works both as an adjective (極端天氣 is extreme weather) and as a noun: 走極端 means to go to extremes. 極 originally meant a crossbeam rafter.

column3: Before an adjective it is a formal way to say extremely: 异常寒冷, 异常安静. On its own as an adjective it means abnormal, mostly in medical or technical writing. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment and was later borrowed for long-lasting.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì yìcháng hánlěng.
column7: Today's weather is extremely cold.
column9: Before an adjective it is a formal way to say extremely: 異常寒冷, 異常安靜. On its own as an adjective it means abnormal, mostly in medical or technical writing. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment and was later borrowed for long-lasting.

column3: The doubled form adds feeling. It usually takes 地 before a verb: 深深地爱 (love deeply), 深深地吸一口气 (take a deep breath).
column6: Tā shēnshēn de xī le yī kǒu qì.
column7: He took a deep breath.
column9: The doubled form adds feeling. It usually takes 地 before a verb: 深深地愛 (love deeply), 深深地吸一口氣 (take a deep breath).

column3: Usually seen before a verb as in 全力支持 and 全力救援, and in the set phrases 尽全力 and 全力以赴 (go all out). 全 shows a whole piece of jade, and 力 is seen either as an arm bending out from the body or as a wooden plough.
column6: Wǒmen huì quánlì zhīchí nǐ.
column7: We will support you with all our strength.
column9: Usually seen before a verb as in 全力支持 and 全力救援, and in the set phrases 盡全力 and 全力以赴 (go all out). 全 shows a whole piece of jade, and 力 is seen either as an arm bending out from the body or as a wooden plough.

column3: Used when something is true in general and even more true of the case at hand: 这个城市很热闹，周末更是人山人海.
column4: 这家店平时人就多，周末更是满座。
column5: 這家店平時人就多，週末更是滿座。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn píngshí rén jiù duō, zhōumò gèngshì mǎnzuò.
column7: This shop is busy on ordinary days, and on weekends every seat is taken.
column9: Used when something is true in general and even more true of the case at hand: 這個城市很熱鬧，週末更是人山人海.

column3: It rarely stands alone: it is the last part of words such as 面膜 (face mask), 耳膜 (eardrum) and 保鲜膜 (plastic wrap).
column6: Zhè céng mó hěn báo.
column7: This layer of film is very thin.
column9: It rarely stands alone: it is the last part of words such as 面膜 (face mask), 耳膜 (eardrum) and 保鮮膜 (plastic wrap).

column3: Typical verbs are 留下 (leave) and 踩 (tread): 留下脚印, 踩出脚印. 印 shows a hand pressing down on a kneeling person.
column4: 雪地上留下了一串脚印。
column5: 雪地上留下了一串腳印。
column6: Xuědì shang liú xià le yī chuàn jiǎoyìn.
column7: A line of footprints was left on the snow.
column9: Typical verbs are 留下 (leave) and 踩 (tread): 留下腳印, 踩出腳印. 印 shows a hand pressing down on a kneeling person.

column3: Besides two hands, 有两手 means to be good at something: 他做菜真有两手. And 两手准备 means to prepare for both outcomes. 手 is a picture of a hand and fingers.
column6: Tā zuò cài zhēn yǒu liǎngshǒu.
column7: He is really good at cooking.
column9: Besides two hands, 有兩手 means to be good at something: 他做菜真有兩手. And 兩手準備 means to prepare for both outcomes. 手 is a picture of a hand and fingers.

column3: Also stands for a friendly manner: 笑脸相迎 means to greet someone with a smile.
column6: Háizi huà le yī gè xiàoliǎn.
column7: The child drew a smiley face.
column9: Also stands for a friendly manner: 笑臉相迎 means to greet someone with a smile.

column3: A medical word for the start of an illness or an attack. 发病率 is the incidence rate. 发 comes from a picture of a bow firing an arrow.
column4: 他是在昨天晚上发病的。
column5: 他是在昨天晚上發病的。
column6: Tā shì zài zuótiān wǎnshang fābìng de.
column7: His illness started last night.
column9: A medical word for the start of an illness or an attack. 發病率 is the incidence rate. 發 comes from a picture of a bow firing an arrow.

column3: Short for 流行性感冒, the full medical name. An ordinary cold is 感冒, and people say 得了流感 or 感染流感 for catching the flu.
column6: Jīnnián dōngtiān liúgǎn hěn yánzhòng.
column7: The flu is bad this winter.
column9: Short for 流行性感冒, the full medical name. An ordinary cold is 感冒, and people say 得了流感 or 感染流感 for catching the flu.

column3: Usually said with 有 or 得: 有心脏病 means to have heart disease, and 心脏病发作 means that a heart attack strikes. 心 is a stylized picture of a heart.
column6: Tā yéye yǒu xīnzàngbìng.
column7: His grandfather has heart disease.
column9: Usually said with 有 or 得: 有心髒病 means to have heart disease, and 心臟病發作 means that a heart attack strikes. 心 is a stylized picture of a heart.

column3: More formal than plain 疼. In speech you say 我肚子疼, while 疼痛 turns up in medical advice, such as 缓解疼痛 (ease pain).
column6: Zhè zhǒng yào kěyǐ huǎnjiě téngtòng.
column7: This medicine can ease the pain.
column9: More formal than plain 疼. In speech you say 我肚子疼, while 疼痛 turns up in medical advice, such as 緩解疼痛 (ease pain).

column3: Also used figuratively for a problem that gives you a headache: 这件事让我很头疼. In Taiwan and the south people usually say 头痛. 头 is the character for head that replaced the older 首, which sounded like 手 (hand).
column6: Zhè jiàn shì zhēn ràng rén tóuténg.
column7: This matter is a real headache.
column9: Also used figuratively for a problem that gives you a headache: 這件事讓我很頭疼. In Taiwan and the south people usually say 頭痛. 頭 is the character for head that replaced the older 首, which sounded like 手 (hand).

column3: A verb-object word, so it takes no object of its own: 他晕车 or 容易晕车. Likewise 晕船 (seasick). 晕 began as a picture of the sun ringed with lines, a halo, and 车 as a carriage seen from above.
column6: Wǒ yī zuò chē jiù yùnchē.
column7: I get carsick as soon as I ride in a car.
column9: A verb-object word, so it takes no object of its own: 他暈車 or 容易暈車. Likewise 暈船 (seasick). 暈 began as a picture of the sun ringed with lines, a halo, and 車 as a carriage seen from above.

column3: Seldom alone. It sits in words such as 昏迷 (coma), 头昏 (dizzy) and 黄昏 (dusk), and 昏过去 is to faint. 昏 is the sun 日 going down beneath 氏: nightfall, twilight.
column4: 他一看到血就昏过去了。
column5: 他一看到血就昏過去了。
column6: Tā yī kàn dào xuè jiù hūn guòqù le.
column7: He fainted the moment he saw blood.
column9: Seldom alone. It sits in words such as 昏迷 (coma), 頭昏 (dizzy) and 黃昏 (dusk), and 昏過去 is to faint. 昏 is the sun 日 going down beneath 氏: nightfall, twilight.

column3: Typical verbs are 包扎 (bandage), 清洗 (clean) and 愈合 (heal): 伤口愈合了.
column6: Yīshēng gěi tā de shāngkǒu xiāodú.
column7: The doctor disinfected his wound.
column9: Typical verbs are 包扎 (bandage), 清洗 (clean) and 癒合 (heal): 傷口癒合了.

column3: A news and official word, mostly about accidents, disasters and war: 伤亡人数 (the number of casualties), 造成伤亡 (cause casualties).
column4: 这次事故没有造成人员伤亡。
column5: 這次事故沒有造成人員傷亡。
column6: Zhè cì shìgù méiyǒu zàochéng rényuán shāngwáng.
column7: This accident caused no casualties.
column9: A news and official word, mostly about accidents, disasters and war: 傷亡人數 (the number of casualties), 造成傷亡 (cause casualties).

column3: In this sense it only appears in words about sleep, such as 睡觉 and 午觉. In 觉得 and 感觉 it is read jué.
column6: Wǒ měi tiān wǎnshang shí diǎn shuì jiào.
column7: I go to sleep at ten every night.
column9: In this sense it only appears in words about sleep, such as 睡覺 and 午覺. In 覺得 and 感覺 it is read jué.

column3: A hospital department: 儿科医生 is a children's doctor, and parents take a sick child to the 儿科.
column4: 孩子发烧了，我们去儿科看看吧。
column5: 孩子發燒了，我們去兒科看看吧。
column6: Háizi fāshāo le, wǒmen qù érkē kànkan ba.
column7: The child has a fever, so let's go to the pediatrics department.
column9: A hospital department: 兒科醫生 is a children's doctor, and parents take a sick child to the 兒科.

column3: Names the whole field and industry rather than one medicine: 医药费 (medical costs), 医药公司. A single medicine is 药.
column4: 他在一家医药公司工作。
column5: 他在一家醫藥公司工作。
column6: Tā zài yī jiā yīyào gōngsī gōngzuò.
column7: He works for a pharmaceutical company.
column9: Names the whole field and industry rather than one medicine: 醫藥費 (medical costs), 醫藥公司. A single medicine is 藥.

column3: The formal word for medicine as a product, seen on packaging, in laws and in shops. In speech people just say 药. 品 is three 口 piled up, standing for various objects.
column4: 这些药品要放在阴凉的地方。
column5: 這些藥品要放在陰涼的地方。
column6: Zhèxiē yàopǐn yào fàng zài yīnliáng de dìfang.
column7: These medicines should be kept in a cool place.
column9: The formal word for medicine as a product, seen on packaging, in laws and in shops. In speech people just say 藥. 品 is three 口 piled up, standing for various objects.

column3: A verb-object word, so it can be split: 治好了病, 给病人治病. A patient who goes to see a doctor is said to 看病. In 病, 丙 also means fire, hence the picture of lying feverishly in bed.
column6: Zhè zhǒng cǎoyào kěyǐ zhìbìng.
column7: This herbal medicine can cure illness.
column9: A verb-object word, so it can be split: 治好了病, 給病人治病. A patient who goes to see a doctor is said to 看病. In 病, 丙 also means fire, hence the picture of lying feverishly in bed.

column3: Found in 急救箱 (first-aid kit), 急救中心 and 急救知识 (first-aid knowledge).
column6: Tā xué guo jíjiù.
column7: He has learned first aid.
column9: Found in 急救箱 (first-aid kit), 急救中心 and 急救知識 (first-aid knowledge).

column3: About getting well again after a long illness or an injury, not a passing cold: 康复治疗 (rehabilitation), and 祝你早日康复 is a get-well wish. 复 originally meant going back, which suits getting back to health.
column6: Zhù nǐ zǎorì kāngfù.
column7: I wish you a speedy recovery.
column9: About getting well again after a long illness or an injury, not a passing cold: 康復治療 (rehabilitation), and 祝你早日康復 is a get-well wish. 復 originally meant going back, which suits getting back to health.

column3: Mostly in compounds and formal contexts: 保健品 (health supplements), 保健操 (health exercises). 保 shows a person carrying a child on the back, and so came to mean to protect.
column6: Tā hěn zhùyì bǎojiàn.
column7: He takes care of his health.
column9: Mostly in compounds and formal contexts: 保健品 (health supplements), 保健操 (health exercises). 保 shows a person carrying a child on the back, and so came to mean to protect.

column3: The topic of old age and retirement: 养老院 (nursing home), 养老金 (pension), 养老保险 (pension insurance). 老 shows a man with long hair, leaning on a cane.
column6: Tā dǎsuàn huí lǎojiā yǎnglǎo.
column7: He plans to retire in his hometown.
column9: The topic of old age and retirement: 養老院 (nursing home), 養老金 (pension), 養老保險 (pension insurance). 老 shows a man with long hair, leaning on a cane.

column3: Used for an economy, a market or nature coming back to life, as well as a patient being revived: 经济复苏, and 万物复苏 in spring.
column6: Chūntiān lái le, wànwù fùsū.
column7: Spring has come and everything comes back to life.
column9: Used for an economy, a market or nature coming back to life, as well as a patient being revived: 經濟復甦, and 萬物復甦 in spring.

column3: The verb for laying is 下: 母鸡下蛋. The male is 公鸡. 母 marks the female of farm animals: 母牛, 母猪.
column6: Mǔjī xià le yī gè dàn.
column7: The hen laid an egg.
column9: The verb for laying is 下: 母雞下蛋. The male is 公雞. 母 marks the female of farm animals: 母牛, 母豬.

column3: 牛 is a picture of a bull's head with two horns and two ears.
column4: 这头奶牛每天产很多奶。
column5: 這頭奶牛每天產很多奶。
column6: Zhè tóu nǎiniú měi tiān chǎn hěn duō nǎi.
column7: This dairy cow gives a lot of milk every day.
column9: 牛 is a picture of a bull's head with two horns and two ears.

column3: Counted with 棵: 一棵果树. Fruit trees are 种 (planted) in a 果园 (orchard). 果 is a picture of fruits on a tree.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ zhòng le jǐ kē guǒshù.
column7: Several fruit trees are planted in the yard.
column9: Counted with 棵: 一棵果樹. Fruit trees are 種 (planted) in a 果園 (orchard). 果 is a picture of fruits on a tree.

column3: Goes before the animal or plant: 野生动物, 野生植物. The opposite is 人工养殖 for animals and 人工栽培 for plants. 生 shows a bud sprouting from the ground.
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu hěn duō yěshēng dòngwù.
column7: There are a lot of wild animals here.
column9: Goes before the animal or plant: 野生動物, 野生植物. The opposite is 人工養殖 for animals and 人工栽培 for plants. 生 shows a bud sprouting from the ground.

column3: It rarely stands alone: it ends words such as 煤矿 (coal mine), 铁矿 (iron ore) and 矿工 (miner).
column6: Tā zài méi kuàng gōngzuò.
column7: He works in a coal mine.
column9: It rarely stands alone: it ends words such as 煤礦 (coal mine), 鐵礦 (iron ore) and 礦工 (miner).

column3: Also used figuratively for hard times: 暴风雨来临前的平静 is the calm before the storm. 雨 is a picture of a cloud with drops of rain falling from it.
column6: Bàofēngyǔ jiù yào lái le.
column7: The storm is about to arrive.
column9: Also used figuratively for hard times: 暴風雨來臨前的平靜 is the calm before the storm. 雨 is a picture of a cloud with drops of rain falling from it.

column3: Weather reports rank it above 大雨, and issue a 暴雨预警 (heavy rain warning). 暴 pairs a tiger 虎 with a weapon 戈: violence.
column6: Zuówǎn xià le yī chǎng bàoyǔ.
column7: There was a downpour last night.
column9: Weather reports rank it above 大雨, and issue a 暴雨預警 (heavy rain warning). 暴 pairs a tiger 虎 with a weapon 戈: violence.

column3: In the news it often means a crisis rather than weather: 金融风暴 is a financial crisis.
column4: 金融风暴影响了很多人。
column5: 金融風暴影響了很多人。
column6: Jīnróng fēngbào yǐngxiǎng le hěn duō rén.
column7: The financial crisis affected many people.
column9: In the news it often means a crisis rather than weather: 金融風暴 is a financial crisis.

column3: Typical phrases are 发洪水 (a flood breaks out) and 洪水泛滥 (floodwaters spread).
column4: 去年夏天这里发了洪水。
column5: 去年夏天這裡發了洪水。
column6: Qùnián xiàtiān zhèlǐ fā le hóngshuǐ.
column7: This place flooded last summer.
column9: Typical phrases are 發洪水 (a flood breaks out) and 洪水泛濫 (floodwaters spread).

column3: Often figurative: dark clouds hanging over a situation, as in 乌云密布 for trouble gathering. The first character began as a picture of a bird, and its sense of black comes from the crow: black as a crow.
column4: 天空布满了乌云，快要下雨了。
column5: 天空布滿了烏雲，快要下雨了。
column6: Tiānkōng bù mǎn le wūyún, kuàiyào xiàyǔ le.
column7: The sky is covered with dark clouds; it is about to rain.
column9: Often figurative: dark clouds hanging over a situation, as in 烏雲密布 for trouble gathering. The first character began as a picture of a bird, and its sense of black comes from the crow: black as a crow.

column3: The second character, in its oldest writing, is a standing man seen from the front, with the head drawn in several ways.
column4: 今天是蓝天白云的好天气。
column5: 今天是藍天白雲的好天氣。
column6: Jīntiān shì lántiān báiyún de hǎo tiānqì.
column7: Today is nice weather, with blue sky and white clouds.
column9: The second character, in its oldest writing, is a standing man seen from the front, with the head drawn in several ways.

column3: Used for weather and in science or industry, as in 低温保存 (keep refrigerated); the opposite is 高温. The second character shows a person bathing in a container full of warm water.
column6: Dīwēn tiānqì yào duō chuān yīfu.
column7: In cold weather you need to wear more clothes.
column9: Used for weather and in science or industry, as in 低溫保存 (keep refrigerated); the opposite is 高溫. The second character shows a person bathing in a container full of warm water.

column3: The subject is a light source such as the sun, the moon or a lamp, and the object is what it lights up; also figurative, like glory shining on someone.
column6: Yángguāng zhàoyào zhe dàdì.
column7: The sunlight shines on the earth.
column9: The subject is a light source such as the sun, the moon or a lamp, and the object is what it lights up; also figurative, like glory shining on someone.

column3: Both a noun (the radiance of the sun, or of an ideal) and an adjective for something glorious, as in 光辉形象. The first character shows fire over a person's head, which stresses the shining of light.
column4: 他的光辉形象永远留在我们心中。
column5: 他的光輝形象永遠留在我們心中。
column6: Tā de guānghuī xíngxiàng yǒngyuǎn liú zài wǒmen xīnzhōng.
column7: His glorious image will stay in our hearts forever.
column9: Both a noun (the radiance of the sun, or of an ideal) and an adjective for something glorious, as in 光輝形象. The first character shows fire over a person's head, which stresses the shining of light.

column3: The second character pictures a valley between two mountain walls.
column6: Shāngǔ lǐ huídàng zhe gēshēng.
column7: Singing echoes through the valley.
column9: The second character pictures a valley between two mountain walls.

column3: On its own it is rare; it mostly turns up in words such as 上坡, 下坡 and 山坡.
column4: 前面有一个坡，骑车要小心。
column5: 前面有一個坡，騎車要小心。
column6: Qiánmiàn yǒu yī gè pō, qí chē yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: There is a slope ahead, so be careful when riding.
column9: On its own it is rare; it mostly turns up in words such as 上坡, 下坡 and 山坡.

column3: 海 is probably related to 晦, "dark": many Zhou texts describe 海 as 晦.
column6: Hǎidǐ yǒu hěn duō qíguài de yú.
column7: There are many strange fish on the seafloor.
column9: 海 is probably related to 晦, "dark": many Zhou texts describe 海 as 晦.

column3: Besides any bay, it is the usual short name for the Persian Gulf region.
column4: 这个海湾风浪很小，适合停船。
column5: 這個海灣風浪很小，適合停船。
column6: Zhège hǎiwān fēnglàng hěn xiǎo, shìhé tíng chuán.
column7: This bay has small waves, so it is good for anchoring boats.
column9: Besides any bay, it is the usual short name for the Persian Gulf region.

column3: Mostly describes places along the coast, before a noun: 沿海城市, 沿海地区.
column6: Shànghǎi shì yī zuò yánhǎi chéngshì.
column7: Shanghai is a coastal city.
column9: Mostly describes places along the coast, before a noun: 沿海城市, 沿海地區.

column3: Beyond water, it also describes anything wavy, such as 波浪形 lines.
column6: Hǎimiàn shàng xiānqǐ le dà bōlàng.
column7: Big waves rose on the sea.
column9: Beyond water, it also describes anything wavy, such as 波浪形 lines.

column3: It is mostly bound inside words: 海洋, 太平洋, and as a prefix meaning foreign or Western, as in 洋人 and 洋快餐. The sense of foreign comes from the Atlantic, home of the Western countries, and was shortened to this character in the 19th century.
column6: Háizimen ài chī yáng kuàicān.
column7: The kids love Western fast food.
column9: It is mostly bound inside words: 海洋, 太平洋, and as a prefix meaning foreign or Western, as in 洋人 and 洋快餐. The sense of foreign comes from the Atlantic, home of the Western countries, and was shortened to this character in the 19th century.

column3: Describes a lucky fit in time, size or amount, placed before the verb: 恰好赶上 means arriving just in time.
column4: 我到车站的时候，车恰好来了。
column5: 我到車站的時候，車恰好來了。
column6: Wǒ dào chēzhàn de shíhou, chē qiàhǎo lái le.
column7: When I got to the station, the bus came just then.
column9: Describes a lucky fit in time, size or amount, placed before the verb: 恰好趕上 means arriving just in time.

column3: Stresses that something is exactly the case, often the opposite of what was expected: 恰恰相反 is "just the opposite".
column4: 我想的和他想的恰恰相反。
column5: 我想的和他想的恰恰相反。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng de hé tā xiǎng de qiàqià xiāngfǎn.
column7: What I think is exactly the opposite of what he thinks.
column9: Stresses that something is exactly the case, often the opposite of what was expected: 恰恰相反 is "just the opposite".

column3: Said of words, methods, timing and measures: 用词恰当 is "well-chosen wording".
column4: 这个词用在这里不太恰当。
column5: 這個詞用在這裡不太恰當。
column6: Zhège cí yòng zài zhèlǐ bù tài qiàdàng.
column7: This word is not quite suitable here.
column9: Said of words, methods, timing and measures: 用詞恰當 is "well-chosen wording".

column3: Despite 容易 "easy" in it, it means it was hard: 好容易才 is "finally, with great difficulty", the same as 好不容易.
column6: Wǒ hǎoróngyì cái mǎi dào piào.
column7: I had a hard time getting a ticket.
column9: Despite 容易 "easy" in it, it means it was hard: 好容易才 is "finally, with great difficulty", the same as 好不容易.

column3: Followed by a verb; the situation that leaves no choice usually comes first. It is close to 只好.
column4: 车坏了，我只得走路回家。
column5: 車壞了，我只得走路回家。
column6: Chē huài le, wǒ zhǐdé zǒulù huí jiā.
column7: The car broke down, so I had to walk home.
column9: Followed by a verb; the situation that leaves no choice usually comes first. It is close to 只好.

column3: Followed by a verb: being so absorbed in one thing that everything else is ignored, often with a reproachful tone.
column4: 他只顾看手机，没听见我说话。
column5: 他只顧看手機，沒聽見我說話。
column6: Tā zhǐgù kàn shǒujī, méi tīngjiàn wǒ shuōhuà.
column7: He was so busy looking at his phone that he didn't hear me.
column9: Followed by a verb: being so absorbed in one thing that everything else is ignored, often with a reproachful tone.

column3: Most often an invitation, "go right ahead": 有问题只管问. It can also mean doing nothing but one thing.
column6: Yǒu shénme wèntí zhǐguǎn wèn wǒ.
column7: If you have any questions, just ask me.
column9: Most often an invitation, "go right ahead": 有問題只管問. It can also mean doing nothing but one thing.

column3: Describes what someone did right away in response to something, so it fits a story but not a command.
column4: 看见老师进来，他赶忙站了起来。
column5: 看見老師進來，他趕忙站了起來。
column6: Kànjiàn lǎoshī jìn lái, tā gǎnmáng zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: Seeing the teacher come in, he quickly stood up.
column9: Describes what someone did right away in response to something, so it fits a story but not a command.

column3: Doing or being the same as before in spite of a change; it goes before the verb.
column6: Xià dà yǔ tā zhàoyàng qù shàngbān.
column7: Even in heavy rain he goes to work as usual.
column9: Doing or being the same as before in spite of a change; it goes before the verb.

column3: Read zhèngdàng it means proper or legitimate (正当理由); read zhèngdāng it means "just when", as in 正当…的时候.
column6: Tā de yāoqiú hěn zhèngdàng.
column7: His request is reasonable.
column9: Read zhèngdàng it means proper or legitimate (正當理由); read zhèngdāng it means "just when", as in 正當…的時候.

column3: Passenger vehicles, as opposed to 货车 for goods; it can be a bus or a train.
column4: 这趟客车每天早上七点开。
column5: 這趟客車每天早上七點開。
column6: Zhè tàng kèchē měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn kāi.
column7: This passenger train leaves at seven every morning.
column9: Passenger vehicles, as opposed to 貨車 for goods; it can be a bus or a train.

column3: Found in 特快列车 for an express train and 特快专递 for express mail.
column4: 这趟特快列车直达北京。
column5: 這趟特快列車直達北京。
column6: Zhè tàng tèkuài lièchē zhídá Běijīng.
column7: This express train goes straight to Beijing.
column9: Found in 特快列車 for an express train and 特快專遞 for express mail.

column3: The legal term in traffic rules for cars and motorcycles; bicycles fall under 非机动车.
column4: 机动车必须让行人先走。
column5: 機動車必須讓行人先走。
column6: Jīdòngchē bìxū ràng xíngrén xiān zǒu.
column7: Motor vehicles must let pedestrians go first.
column9: The legal term in traffic rules for cars and motorcycles; bicycles fall under 非機動車.

column3: An idiom for staying up late to study or work, especially before an exam or deadline; it has nothing to do with driving.
column6: Kǎoshì qián tā tiāntiān kāiyèchē.
column7: Before exams he stays up late every day.
column9: An idiom for staying up late to study or work, especially before an exam or deadline; it has nothing to do with driving.

column3: In Taiwan the word also means to appear publicly in support of a candidate, and a railway platform is usually 月台.
column4: 请站在站台的黄线后面。
column5: 請站在站臺的黃線後面。
column6: Qǐng zhàn zài zhàntái de huángxiàn hòumiàn.
column7: Please stand behind the yellow line on the platform.
column9: In Taiwan the word also means to appear publicly in support of a candidate, and a railway platform is usually 月臺.

column3: On mainland trains it comes in 硬卧 (hard sleeper) and 软卧 (soft sleeper).
column4: 我买了一张去北京的卧铺票。
column5: 我買了一張去北京的臥鋪票。
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī zhāng qù Běijīng de wòpù piào.
column7: I bought a sleeper ticket to Beijing.
column9: On mainland trains it comes in 硬臥 (hard sleeper) and 軟臥 (soft sleeper).

column3: Beyond rails, it means an orbit, and figuratively a settled course: 走上轨道 is "get on track".
column4: 公司的业务已经走上了轨道。
column5: 公司的業務已經走上了軌道。
column6: Gōngsī de yèwù yǐjīng zǒu shàng le guǐdào.
column7: The company's business is already on track.
column9: Beyond rails, it means an orbit, and figuratively a settled course: 走上軌道 is "get on track".

column3: A collective word for ships in general, so it is not counted with a number: 来往船只 is "passing ships"; for one ship say 一艘船.
column6: Gǎngkǒu lǐ tíng zhe hěn duō chuánzhī.
column7: Many ships are docked in the harbor.
column9: A collective word for ships in general, so it is not counted with a number: 來往船隻 is "passing ships"; for one ship say 一艘船.

column3: Also figurative: 渡过难关 is "get through a hard time", and the ferry crossing is a 渡口.
column4: 我们坐船渡过了那条河。
column5: 我們坐船渡過了那條河。
column6: Wǒmen zuò chuán dù guò le nà tiáo hé.
column7: We crossed the river by boat.
column9: Also figurative: 渡過難關 is "get through a hard time", and the ferry crossing is a 渡口.

column3: Usually a spaceship, short for 宇宙飞船; it can also be an airship.
column4: 飞船成功降落在地球上。
column5: 飛船成功降落在地球上。
column6: Fēichuán chénggōng jiàngluò zài dìqiú shàng.
column7: The spacecraft landed safely on Earth.
column9: Usually a spaceship, short for 宇宙飛船; it can also be an airship.

column3: A mainland word for an astronaut (China's own are officially 航天员); in Taiwan 太空人 is the usual word. The second character first meant eaves and stretched to abode and territory.
column4: 宇航员在空间站工作了半年。
column5: 宇航員在空間站工作了半年。
column6: Yǔhángyuán zài kōngjiānzhàn gōngzuò le bàn nián.
column7: The astronaut worked on the space station for half a year.
column9: A mainland word for an astronaut (China's own are officially 航天員); in Taiwan 太空人 is the usual word. The second character first meant eaves and stretched to abode and territory.

column3: Short for 安全检查, at airports and stations; also a verb: 过安检 is "go through security".
column4: 过安检时要把水拿出来。
column5: 過安檢時要把水拿出來。
column6: Guò ānjiǎn shí yào bǎ shuǐ ná chūlái.
column7: When going through security, take out your water.
column9: Short for 安全檢查, at airports and stations; also a verb: 過安檢 is "go through security".

column3: Common in notices and news: 绿色出行 "low-carbon travel", 出行方式 "way of getting around".
column4: 下雨天出行要注意安全。
column5: 下雨天出行要注意安全。
column6: Xiàyǔ tiān chūxíng yào zhùyì ānquán.
column7: Be careful when you go out on rainy days.
column9: Common in notices and news: 綠色出行 "low-carbon travel", 出行方式 "way of getting around".
